examples.source: Ofcom Connected Nations Spring 2026
examples.verified_fact: UK residential gigabit-capable availability is 89% and full-fibre availability is 82%.
examples.allowed_use: National aggregate sanity check only
examples.forbidden_use: Do not assign these national percentages to a postcode or parcel.

examples.source: ONS Postcode Directory May 2026 hosted table
examples.verified_fact: Quarterly directory linking current and terminated UK postcodes to statutory and statistical geographies.
examples.allowed_use: Postcode normalization and geography crosswalk QA
examples.forbidden_use: No broadband coverage value substitution.

examples.source: Online ONS Postcode Directory Live
examples.verified_fact: Digital vector centroids for live UK postcodes as at May 2026.
examples.allowed_use: Postcode centroid and live-status QA
examples.forbidden_use: Never replace canonical parcel geometry.

examples.source: National Statistics Postcode Lookup May 2026 hosted table
examples.verified_fact: Relates current and terminated postcodes to current geographies using best-fit allocation from 2021 Census Output Areas, with stated exceptions.
examples.allowed_use: Secondary geography allocation cross-check
examples.forbidden_use: Not an exact parcel boundary or broadband measurement.

examples.source: OS Code-Point Open
examples.verified_fact: Open dataset of current postcode units in Great Britain, updated every three months.
examples.allowed_use: Fallback postcode location QA
examples.forbidden_use: No premise-level broadband measurement or parcel assignment.

examples.source: Ofcom Connected Nations FAQs
examples.verified_fact: Fixed broadband coverage downloads describe maximum available service; performance data describes active-connection speeds and is a separate product.
examples.allowed_use: Treat Spring 2026 postcode values as availability coverage only
examples.forbidden_use: Do not label availability percentages as measured customer speed or performance.

examples.source: Ofcom Connected Nations FAQs
examples.verified_fact: Since the July 2024 methodology change, Ofcom considers average download-speed analysis robust to local-authority level, not postcode level.
examples.allowed_use: Keep postcode rows as coverage proxies and leave performance/parcel scores null
examples.forbidden_use: Do not infer postcode or parcel measured speed from Connected Nations performance analysis.

examples.source: Ofcom Spring 2026 fixed coverage V2 schema
examples.verified_fact: Ofcom corrected the CW file that duplicated CV and the MK file that duplicated ME, then renamed all 121 all-premises postcode files from r1 to r2.
examples.allowed_use: Require r2 names and verify CW!=CV and MK!=ME by SHA-256 before any join
examples.forbidden_use: Do not accept the superseded internal r1 postcode files or a package retaining either duplicate defect.

examples.source: Ofcom Spring 2026 fixed coverage V2 schema
examples.verified_fact: The postcode field has spaces removed and postcode_space uses one space before the inward code.
examples.allowed_use: Require exact UK postcode syntax, exact one-space postcode_space formatting and matching normalized values
examples.forbidden_use: Do not silently accept malformed spacing or conflicting postcode identifiers.

examples.source: Ofcom Spring 2026 fixed coverage V2 schema
examples.verified_fact: SFBB, UFBB and gigabit fields are availability percentages; the unable-to-receive-30 field is defined for matched premises, while unable-to-receive-decent fixed-or-FWA includes unmatched and zero-speed records.
examples.allowed_use: Preserve the documented denominator for each metric in validation/readback metadata
examples.forbidden_use: Do not treat unable-30 as the exact complement of SFBB or mix the two denominators.

examples.source: Ofcom Spring 2026 fixed coverage V2 schema
examples.verified_fact: Postcode and output-area files contain gigabit-capable coverage but not full-fibre coverage due to commercial confidentiality; coverage is fixed-line except fields explicitly referring to FWA.
examples.allowed_use: Reject unexpected postcode-level full-fibre columns and label explicit FWA fields separately
examples.forbidden_use: Do not infer postcode full-fibre availability or describe every field as fixed-plus-FWA coverage.

examples.source: Ofcom fixed coverage threshold definitions
examples.verified_fact: SFBB is coverage at 30 Mbit/s or greater, UFBB fields are coverage at 100 and 300 Mbit/s or greater, and gigabit is gigabit-capable service.
examples.allowed_use: Validate each postcode row as SFBB30 >= UFBB100 >= UFBB300 >= Gigabit before joining
examples.forbidden_use: Do not accept a higher-speed coverage percentage exceeding its lower-speed parent threshold.

examples.source: Ofcom Spring 2026 fixed coverage V2 file table
examples.verified_fact: The all-premises postcode product contains 121 r2 files in the postcode_files folder and 1,741,096 data rows.
examples.allowed_use: Require the exact folder level, file count and row count before any postcode join
examples.forbidden_use: Do not mix residential postcode files, files from another folder level or partial extracts into the all-premises join.

examples.source: Ofcom Spring 2026 fixed coverage V2 field matrix
examples.verified_fact: All Premises, All Matched Premises and Number of premises fields are marked as unavailable for postcode files, while postcode coverage outputs are percentage fields.
examples.allowed_use: Reject wrong-level premise-count columns and validate every percentage column as finite and within 0-100
examples.forbidden_use: Do not interpret a local-authority/output-area count schema as a postcode schema or ignore invalid unused percentage columns.

examples.source: Ofcom Spring 2026 download link and V2 PDF
examples.verified_fact: The downloadable outer archive retains an r1 transport filename while the corrected all-premises postcode payload is explicitly renamed to 121 r2 CSV files.
examples.allowed_use: Accept the official outer transport filename only after runtime ZIP and internal V2 validation succeeds
examples.forbidden_use: Do not reject the corrected package solely because the outer archive name contains r1, and do not accept internal r1 postcode CSVs.

examples.source: Ofcom Spring 2026 page readbacks
examples.verified_fact: Current official-page readbacks expose conflicting rounded display labels of 32.2 MB and 32.3 MB for the same fixed-broadband archive.
examples.allowed_use: Record both observations as non-authoritative display metadata
examples.forbidden_use: Do not require an exact rounded page label as a package integrity or revision gate.

examples.source: Ofcom Spring 2026 download publication
examples.verified_fact: No official SHA-256 checksum was found on the publication page or V2 data-description PDF.
examples.allowed_use: Compute and preserve SHA-256 from the downloaded bytes and bind it to PK signature, byte count and internal V2 validation
examples.forbidden_use: Do not invent an official checksum or claim package identity from URL, filename or displayed size alone.

examples.source: Microsoft Learn Invoke-WebRequest PowerShell 5.1 and 7.6
examples.verified_fact: OutFile writes the response body to a file; PassThru is needed for pipeline output, but Microsoft documents that the OutFile plus PassThru combination can leave the file empty.
examples.allowed_use: Keep the production ZIP download on OutFile without PassThru and validate the resulting bytes directly
examples.forbidden_use: Do not add PassThru merely to capture response metadata when it can invalidate the downloaded file.

examples.source: ZIP container safety contract
examples.verified_fact: Archive entry names can be validated before extraction for absolute paths, parent traversal, case-folded duplicates, encryption and symlink metadata.
examples.allowed_use: Reject unsafe container structure before Expand-Archive and before any CSV read
examples.forbidden_use: Do not treat a PK signature alone as proof that archive extraction is safe.

examples.source: Ofcom V2 payload identity plus ZIP safety contract
examples.verified_fact: The corrected payload requires zero internal postcode r1 files and exactly 121 unique r2 postcode areas under postcode_files.
examples.allowed_use: Bind the pre-extraction container audit SHA-256 into the same run provenance chain as the official ZIP and V2 report
examples.forbidden_use: Do not allow a safe-looking container audit from another run or package to satisfy the current extraction.
